mainTopic: טובת הנאה with תרומה vs. מתנות כהונה, and the leniencies of תרומת חוצה לארץ
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא: the owner of produce keeps טובת הנאה, the small benefit of choosing which כהן gets his תרומה. A ישראל may pay the owner a סלע to send the תרומה to his grandson, a כהן, but a כהן may not pay to get gifts for himself. The גמרא asks why the ברייתא mentions only תרומה and not מתנות כהונה. It answers that תרומה has קדושת הגוף and can never be redeemed, so no one will be misled. מתנות כהונה have only קדושת דמים, so a payment might make people think they were redeemed and treat them like חולין. The גמרא then lists leniencies for תרומת חוצה לארץ, which is only rabbinic. A כהן who helps at the threshing floor may receive it. It is nullified by a simple majority, as shown by רבה and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע. One may eat the produce first and separate the תרומה later. שמואל also rules that it is forbidden only to someone whose impurity comes from his own body, and only for eating, not touching. רבינא draws from this a practical rule about a נדה separating חלה. The amud ends with a story on a boat: a woman asks whether a טמא מת may immerse and eat תרומת חוצה לארץ, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The owner keeps the benefit of choice
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends its rule: טובת הנאה belongs to the owner of the produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: The benefit of discretion belongs to the owners.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of a ברייתא that began on the previous amud. It concludes that the owner keeps טובת הנאה, the right to pick which כהן gets his gifts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תרומה itself belongs to the כהנים as a group. The owner still keeps one small thing: he decides which particular כהן receives it. That right of choice has a tiny value, and it is called טובת הנאה.

keyTerms.meaning: The small benefit of choosing who receives a gift
The owners of the produce

steps.confusionAlert: טובת הנאה does not mean the owner owns the תרומה. He owns only the right to choose which כהן receives it.

phrases.english: The benefit of discretion belongs to the owners.
phrases.notes: This is the end of a ברייתא that started on the previous amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes a ברייתא begun on the previous amud
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The owner of the produce keeps טובת הנאה, the right to choose which כהן gets his תרומה.

steps.title: A case showing how the benefit of choice works
steps.stepSummary: A ישראל may pay the owner a סלע to give the תרומה to the ישראל's grandson, a כהן. A כהן paying the owner for the same thing is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does this work? A ישראל separated תרומה from his pile of grain. Another ישראל found him and said: 'Take this סלע, and give the תרומה to my daughter's son, who is a כהן.' This is permitted. But if a כהן paid in order to get it for a כהן, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a real-life example of טובת הנאה. Someone may pay the owner for his right of choice, but only if the payer is not a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ישראל pays only for the owner's right to choose. That shows the choice has real value. A כהן may not do this, because a כהן paying to receive his priestly gifts looks like he is buying them, and that is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? (introduces an example)
The portion of produce given to a כהן
A pile of threshed grain
A coin worth four זוזים
My daughter's son

steps.whyThisMatters: The סלע in this case is worth four זוזים. That is the 'four זוזים' the גמרא refers to in step 5, when it explains why מתנות כהונה were left out.

phrases.english: How so?
An Israelite who separated teruma from his grain pile,
and another Israelite found him and said to him:
"Here, take this sela for yourself,
and give it to my daughter's son, a priest" — it is permitted.
If it was a priest paying for a priest — it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: A כהן may not pay to obtain his own gifts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the rule of טובת הנאה with a concrete case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ישראל may pay for the owner's right of choice. A כהן may not.

steps.title: Why does the ברייתא leave out the priestly meat gifts?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא speaks only of תרומה and does not also say this about מתנות כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason the תנא did not mention מתנות כהונה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the ברייתא mentions only תרומה. It asks why the ברייתא did not apply the same rule to מתנות כהונה (the זרוע, לחיים, and קיבה from an animal).
steps.deeperAnalysis: מתנות כהונה are also gifts the owner chooses which כהן to give, so we would expect the same rule to apply. The leaving-out looks deliberate, and the גמרא wants to know the reason.

keyTerms.meaning: The author of the ברייתא
What is the reason?
Priestly gifts from a slaughtered animal: the זרוע, לחיים, and קיבה

phrases.english: And the tanna, what is the reason
that he does not state the gifts of the priesthood?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the ברייתא limited its case to תרומה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the ברייתא did not apply טובת הנאה to מתנות כהונה as well

steps.title: תרומה cannot be redeemed, so nobody will be misled
steps.stepSummary: תרומה has קדושת הגוף and can never be redeemed. Selling the right to give it will therefore not confuse anyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: He could tell you: תרומה has holiness in its very body. Since it can never be redeemed, people will not make a mistake about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer by explaining why selling the right of choice is safe with תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תרומה is holy in itself (קדושת הגוף), and there is no way to redeem it. Everyone knows money cannot remove its holiness. So when a סלע changes hands, no one will think the תרומה became ordinary food.

keyTerms.meaning: Holiness built into the item itself
Can be redeemed (made non-holy through money)
To make a mistake

phrases.english: He could have said to you:
Teruma, which has inherent sanctity,
since it cannot be redeemed —
people will not come to err with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the question in step 3
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: With תרומה there is no risk of error, because it has קדושת הגוף and cannot be redeemed.

steps.title: Priestly gifts might be mistaken for redeemed food
steps.stepSummary: מתנות כהונה have only קדושת דמים. People might think the four-זוז payment redeemed them and start treating them like חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: But these gifts have only monetary holiness, so people might make a mistake about them. They might think the gifts' holiness was redeemed for four זוזים, and come to treat them like ordinary food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer by explaining why the תנא chose not to mention מתנות כהונה in this rule. If he had, people might get confused about their holiness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מתנות כהונה have a weaker holiness tied to their value (קדושת דמים), and a כהן may even sell them. If a סלע (four זוזים) were paid for them, people might think the money redeemed them. They would then eat them carelessly, like חולין, even though a כהן must eat his gifts in a dignified way (roasted and with seasoning, see חולין קלב:).

keyTerms.meaning: Holiness tied to the item's monetary value
Four זוזים, the value of one סלע
Ordinary, non-holy food

steps.whatToRemember: With תרומה (קדושת הגוף), the owner's right of choice can be sold safely. With מתנות כהונה (קדושת דמים), a payment might make people think the holiness was redeemed. That is why the ברייתא mentions only תרומה.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean מתנות כהונה are not holy gifts. Because their holiness is the weaker monetary kind, a payment could make people wrongly think they became ordinary food.

phrases.english: These, since they have monetary sanctity,
people may come to err with them,
thinking that their sanctity can be redeemed for four zuz,
phrases.notes: Four זוזים is the one סלע from the case in step 2.

phrases.english: and they will come to treat them as non-sacred food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the contrast begun in step 4
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because מתנות כהונה have only קדושת דמים, paying for them could lead people to think they were redeemed and to treat them like חולין.

steps.title: A helping כהן may receive תרומה from outside ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that the ban on a כהן המסייע בבית הגרנות does not apply to תרומת חוצה לארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: תרומה from outside ארץ ישראל does not have the problem of a כהן who helps out at the threshing floors.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רבא. A כהן who helps at the threshing floor may receive תרומת חוצה לארץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a כהן may not help a farmer at the threshing floor in order to get the תרומה. That looks like he is being paid for his work with holy gifts, which disgraces the gifts. רבא says this concern does not apply to תרומת חוצה לארץ, because it is only a rabbinic obligation and is treated more lightly.

keyTerms.meaning: תרומה separated from produce grown outside ארץ ישראל. It is a rabbinic obligation.
A כהן who helps the farmer with his work
The threshing floors, where grain is processed and תרומה is separated
It does not carry the problem of

steps.whyThisMatters: This opens a list of leniencies that all come from the same idea: תרומת חוצה לארץ is a weaker, rabbinic form of תרומה.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Teruma from outside the Land —
does not have the issue of
a priest who assists at the threshing floors.
phrases.notes: Normally, giving תרומה to such a כהן looks like paying him wages with holy gifts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of benefiting from the giving of תרומה to a related leniency for תרומת חוצה לארץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The prohibition of כהן המסייע בבית הגרנות does not apply to תרומת חוצה לארץ.

steps.title: רב חמא gave this תרומה to his servant
steps.stepSummary: A story shows רבא's ruling being followed: רב חמא gave תרומת חוצה לארץ to his servant, who was a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חמא would give it to his attendant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבא's ruling with a real-life practice. רב חמא gave תרומת חוצה לארץ to his servant, a כהן who worked for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The servant was helping רב חמא, so receiving the תרומה was like receiving payment for his help. With תרומה from ארץ ישראל this would be forbidden. רב חמא's practice shows that with תרומת חוצה לארץ it is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Would give
His attendant or servant

phrases.english: Rav Chama would give it to his attendant.
phrases.notes: The attendant was a כהן, and the תרומה served as a kind of payment for his help.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's ruling with a practical case.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that a helping כהן may receive תרומת חוצה לארץ
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of רב חמא with his servant

steps.title: תרומה from outside ארץ ישראל is cancelled by a simple majority
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that תרומת חוצה לארץ mixed into regular produce is nullified by a simple majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: תרומה from outside ארץ ישראל is nullified in a majority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second leniency, from שמואל. If תרומת חוצה לארץ gets mixed into more regular produce than תרומה, the mixture is treated as regular produce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Regular תרומה is only nullified when there is a hundred times as much חולין, the rule of one in a hundred and one. שמואל says that for תרומת חוצה לארץ a simple majority is enough. This is again because its holiness is only rabbinic.

keyTerms.meaning: Is nullified, so it loses its separate status inside a mixture
In a majority, meaning more than half

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with regular תרומה. Regular תרומה needs a hundred parts of חולין to be nullified. Only תרומת חוצה לארץ is nullified by a simple majority.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
Teruma from outside the Land —
is nullified in a majority.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: תְּרוּמַת חוּצָה לָאָרֶץ — בְּטֵילָה בְּרוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second leniency for תרומת חוצה לארץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תרומת חוצה לארץ is nullified by a simple majority, not one in a hundred and one.

steps.title: רבה nullified it on purpose and ate it while impure
steps.stepSummary: רבה, a כהן, would deliberately nullify תרומת חוצה לארץ in a majority and eat it while he was impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה would nullify it in a majority, and eat it during his days of impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows שמואל's rule in practice. רבה used the majority rule on purpose and then ate the mixture even while he was טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With regular תרומה this would be forbidden twice over. First, one may not nullify something forbidden on purpose. Second, a טמא כהן may not eat תרומה. רבה's practice shows how lightly תרומת חוצה לארץ was treated: he could deliberately turn it into regular produce and eat it while impure.

keyTerms.meaning: He would nullify it, actively and on purpose
The days when he was ritually impure
The general rule that one may not nullify something forbidden on purpose

phrases.english: Rabba would nullify it in a majority,
phrases.notes: He did this deliberately, which is not allowed with regular תרומה.

phrases.english: and eat it during his days of impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows שמואל's majority rule being applied in practice, and on purpose.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling that תרומת חוצה לארץ is nullified in a majority

steps.title: רב הונא's method for nullifying תרומה wine
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע would mix one jug of תרומה wine into two jugs of regular wine and take out one jug. After that, he added one jug and took out one jug each time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע: when he happened to get תרומה wine, he would pour in two jugs of regular wine and one jug of תרומה wine, and take out one. From then on, he would pour in one and take out one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second story showing the majority rule in practice. רב הונא set up an ongoing system in a vat to nullify תרומה wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first, one jug of תרומה mixed with two jugs of חולין is a minority, so it is nullified. He then drank one jug's worth, which left two jugs that now count as חולין. Each new jug of תרומה wine poured in was again outnumbered two to one, so the same cycle could repeat forever.

keyTerms.meaning: It happened to come to him
Wine
A jug or vessel
Regular, non-holy produce
Takes out

phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua,
when teruma wine would come his way,
would pour two jugs of non-sacred wine
and one jug of teruma wine,
and take out one.
From then on,
he would pour one and take out one.
phrases.notes: The two jugs left in the vat count as חולין, so each new jug of תרומה is always a minority.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, כִּי מִתְרְמֵי לֵיהּ חַמְרָא דִּתְרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another practical case of using the majority rule, this time as a repeating system.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's majority rule for תרומת חוצה לארץ
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע

steps.title: Eat first and separate the תרומה later
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that with produce from outside ארץ ישראל, one may eat it and separate the תרומה afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: with תרומה from outside ארץ ישראל, one eats as he goes, and afterward separates the תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another leniency from שמואל, his second about תרומת חוצה לארץ. Produce from outside ארץ ישראל may be eaten before the תרומה is taken off, as long as the תרומה is separated from what is left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ארץ ישראל, untithed produce is טבל and may not be eaten until תרומה is separated. For produce from outside ארץ ישראל, שמואל allows eating first. He relies on the תרומה being separated later from the remaining produce.

keyTerms.meaning: Keeps eating as he goes
Separates the תרומה
Produce from which תרומה has not yet been separated. In ארץ ישראל it is forbidden to eat.

steps.whatToRemember: תרומת חוצה לארץ is rabbinic, so it gets several leniencies. A helping כהן may receive it. It is nullified by a simple majority. One may eat the produce first and separate the תרומה later.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
Teruma from outside the Land —
one eats as he goes,
and afterward separates.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: תְּרוּמַת חוּצָה לָאָרֶץ, אוֹכֵל וְהוֹלֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another leniency from שמואל about תרומת חוצה לארץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Produce from outside ארץ ישראל may be eaten first, with the תרומה separated afterward.

steps.title: Only impurity from one's own body forbids eating תרומת חוצה לארץ
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that תרומת חוצה לארץ is forbidden only to someone whose impurity comes from his own body, and only for eating, not for touching.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: תרומת חוצה לארץ is forbidden only to a person whose impurity comes out of his own body. And this applies only to eating it. But touching it is no problem for us.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives another lenient ruling about תרומה from outside ארץ ישראל. He limits who is forbidden to eat it, and he limits what is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally any impure כהן may not eat תרומה. שמואל says that for תרומת חוצה לארץ, only impurity that comes from the body itself counts, like a בעל קרי, a זב, or a נדה. Impurity from outside, like touching a dead body, does not forbid it. Even body-impurity only forbids eating, so touching is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity that comes out of a person's own body (for example בַּעַל קֶרִי, זָב, נִדָּה)
And this applies only to... (a phrase that limits a ruling)
Eating
Touching
We have no problem with it

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up two later moves. רבינא's practical rule about a נדה separating חלה depends on it, and so does the woman's question about a טמא מת.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
phrases.notes: Another ruling from שמואל, continuing his earlier lenient rulings.

phrases.english: Teruma from outside the Land is not forbidden

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בְּמִי שֶׁהַטּוּמְאָה יוֹצְאָה עָלָיו מִגּוּפוֹ,
phrases.english: except to one whose impurity comes out of his body,
phrases.notes: For example a בעל קרי or a נדה. A טמא מת is not included.

phrases.english: and this applies only to eating,
but touching — we have no problem with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third lenient ruling from שמואל about תרומת חוצה לארץ, this time about impurity.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תרומת חוצה לארץ is forbidden only to someone with impurity from his own body, and only for eating. Touching is permitted.

steps.title: A נדה may separate חלה outside ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רבינא applies שמואל's rule: a נדה may separate חלה, which a young כהן eats. If no young כהן is available, she burns it and separates a second piece that even an adult כהן may eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Therefore, a נדה may separate חלה, and a young כהן eats it. If there is no young כהן, she takes it on the tip of a skewer and throws it into the oven. Then she separates another piece of חלה, so that the law of חלה will not be forgotten, and an adult כהן eats that one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא draws a practical rule from שמואל's ruling about how חלה is handled outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since touching is allowed, a נדה may separate the חלה herself. Eating is still forbidden to anyone with body-impurity, so only a young כהן, who has never had a קרי and is pure, may eat it. If there is none, the main חלה is burned. A second piece is then taken only as a reminder of the law of חלה, and since it is just a reminder, even an adult כהן may eat it.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore (draws a practical result from a rule)
Separates (literally 'cuts off') the חלה portion from the dough
A young כהן, below the age of קרי, so he is pure
The tip of a skewer

keyTerms.term: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלֹא תִּשְׁתַּכַּח תּוֹרַת חַלָּה
keyTerms.meaning: So that the law of חלה will not be forgotten

steps.confusionAlert: Here כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל does NOT mean the High Priest. It simply means an adult כהן, the opposite of the כֹּהֵן קָטָן mentioned just before.
steps.whatToRemember: Outside ארץ ישראל, touching תרומה or חלה is allowed even with body-impurity, but eating is not. That is why a נדה may separate חלה, while only a pure young כהן may eat the main portion.

phrases.english: Ravina said: Therefore,
a menstruating woman may separate challa,
phrases.notes: She may, because touching is permitted according to שמואל.

phrases.english: and a minor priest eats it,
phrases.notes: He has no body-impurity, so he may eat it.

phrases.english: and if there is no minor priest —
she takes it on the tip of a skewer,
and throws it into the oven,
and then she separates another challa,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלֹא תִּשְׁתַּכַּח תּוֹרַת חַלָּה,
phrases.english: so that the law of challa will not be forgotten,
and an adult priest eats it.
phrases.notes: Since this second piece is only a reminder, an adult כהן may eat it even if he is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies שמואל's rule (touching is allowed, eating is forbidden with body-impurity) to the practical case of חלה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נדה may separate חלה, and a young כהן eats it. Without a young כהן, the main חלה is burned, and a second reminder-חלה is separated, which an adult כהן may eat.

steps.title: On a boat, a woman asks whether a טמא מת may immerse and eat תרומת חוצה לארץ
steps.stepSummary: While traveling on a boat, a woman asks רב נחמן and רמי בר חמא whether a טמא מת may immerse and then eat תרומת חוצה לארץ. רב נחמן turns to רמי בר חמא to respond.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן, רב עמרם, and רמי בר חמא were traveling on a boat. רב עמרם went up to relieve himself. A certain woman came before them and said to them: A person who is טמא מת, may he immerse and then eat תרומת חוצה לארץ? רב נחמן said to רמי בר חמא:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story in which a practical question is asked about a טמא מת and תרומת חוצה לארץ. The last line is a setup: רב נחמן is about to speak, and his words come on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question connects directly to שמואל's ruling, since a טמא מת has impurity from outside his body, not from it. The woman wants to know whether immersing in a מקוה is enough for him to eat this תרומה, even though his seven-day purification is not finished. The answer has not been given yet.
